message:
Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer, Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, the grown array and the staged load now balance with margin for control. In plain words the sun covers one household day with a kettle spare while the box leaks less than harvest heat. Daily yield 13.5 kilowatt-hour per day in the grown-array yield calc (E83) covers daily load 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day in the steady plus staged pull-down estimate (E58) leaving margin 0.300 kilowatt-hour per day in the daily margin calc (E86), about one household daily use so everyday scale holds, with conduction 203 watt in the conduction estimate (E41) and door loss 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57) inside staged average 615 watt in the revised steady-load simulation (E28).

Enclosure and Structural Designer, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, the two masses for one box are reconciled and the split array fits the roof limit. In plain words one small car on six feet stays well below soft soil and nine sails need screws. Grown total 1840 kilogram in the grown mass calc (E87) supersedes 1780 kilogram in the summed chamber mass budget (E66), giving 18.8 kilopascal in the grown pad pressure calc (E89) superseding 18.2 kilopascal in the pad pressure check (E68) and still below 150 kilopascal soil in Structural Design Calculation Sheet | PDF | Strength Of Materials | Precast Concrete (E62), with nine-module footprint 17.6 square metres in the nine-module footprint calc (E84) from module size in PRBS 400W Monocrystalline Photovoltaic Panels | Commercial & High-Performance (E64) split as 2 on roof plus 7 on ground in the grown split-array sketch (E85) with wind uplift like 673 kilogram in the uplift calc (E90) held by screw anchors.

Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer, your four ready votes on version one are answered and no blocking objection is open. In plain words counted crates through one door by day with battery plus ice by night close the working chain. Holding 1000 kilogram in the total produce mass estimate (E49) as 50 crates in the crates for 1 tonne check (E77) staged as 12.5 crates per day in the daily crates check (E78) through 900 millimetre door in Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) under 8-opening discipline keeps Photovoltaic (PV, solar electricity) plus Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4, lithium battery chemistry) with Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT, solar optimizer) and probe control inside that daily balance, leaving full-tonne heat 25.0 kilowatt-hour in the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26) staged as 6.20 kilowatt-hour per batch in that revised steady-load simulation (E28) as the named 43 degree pull-down bench test on built hardware, not a block.

RECORD: Proposal version one stands with grown split array with battery bank with monoblock cooling with insulated box with racked crates with probe thermostat, numbers that stand are 1000 kg (E49) as 50 crates (E77) staged 12.5 per day (E78), yield 13.5 kilowatt-hour per day (E83) against load 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day (E58) margin 0.300 kilowatt-hour per day (E86), conduction 203 watt (E41) plus door 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day (E57) inside 615 watt (E28), grown mass 1840 kg (E87) giving 18.8 kilopascal (E89) below 150 kilopascal (E62) with 17.6 square metre nine-module split 2 plus 7 (E84, E85), still open only 43 degree pull-down bench test needing built hardware owed to test team.
Note on Solar Energy Systems Engineer: closed solar-only balance with grown split yield and night store logic.
Note on Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer: closed staged load, door leak method, and service refrigerant within budget.
Note on Enclosure and Structural Designer: closed grown mass, soil pressure, split footings, and wind anchorage.
Note on Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist: closed counted crate workflow, door ergonomics, and fee-funded discipline.
My position is ready, because daily energy, chamber leak, mass, and interfaces reconcile with only a hardware bench test left.
